passage:
A developer created an app to record family recipes. Users could upload photos, ingredients, cooking steps, and voice recordings from older relatives.
Many young people used the app before holidays. They discovered that family recipes often had unclear measures: "a little," "until soft," or "when it smells right."
The app allowed notes and videos, not just numbers.
A student used it to record her grandfather making soup. Later, when she cooked alone, his voice guided her through the steps.
The app showed that technology can protect tradition if it records more than data. It must also keep tone, habit, and memory.
